title: The Archbishop's Dinner
notebook: Renek says the Church runs 400 schools and educates 60,000 children. Its boilers are cold.
Renek wants funding restored. Church teachers have had no raise in five years.
Vyktor: Renek will mobilize the Church's 4 million faithful against the constitutional reforms unless paid.

narrative.text: Archbishop Renek invites you to a private dinner at his residence. The wine is excellent, the food is austere, and the conversation is a minefield. After the soup, Renek sets down his glass and looks at you with the practiced warmth of a man who wants something.

Chancellor, the Church runs 400 schools in this Republic. We educate 60,000 children. But our boilers are cold, our roofs leak, and our teachers haven't had a raise in five years. The previous government starved us. I am asking you to restore our funding.

He is also hinting, very politely, that if you refuse, the Church will mobilize its 4 million faithful against your constitutional reforms. It is a shakedown, Chancellor. He is holding the referendum hostage for a check.

Renek smiles like a saint and negotiates like a thug. I need the Church's support for the constitution, but I cannot let them think they can dictate terms to the state. If I pay, I look weak. If I refuse, the referendum fails.

choices.text: Restore the full funding. Buy the Church's support for the referendum.
Refuse. The state does not pay bribes. We will win the referendum without the Church.
Counter-offer: State funding, but the schools become secular. The Church loses control.
